subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace by reduction with which substance?
questions.explain: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon reduces iron oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure on a gaseous equilibrium shifts it towards:
options: The side with fewer gas molecules
The side with more gas molecules
questions.explain: Le Chatelier: higher pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce pressure.

questions.q: How does galvanising protect iron from rusting?
options: By coating it with a layer of zinc
By adding carbon to the iron
questions.explain: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which acts as both a barrier and sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the least reactive?
questions.explain: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, making it the least reactive listed.

questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, what happens to the copper oxide?
questions.explain: The copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced.

questions.q: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium will:
options: Shift the equilibrium to the reactants
Shift the equilibrium to the products
Reach equilibrium faster without changing the position
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached sooner but its position is unchanged.

questions.q: What happens to a catalyst during a reaction?
options: It is chemically unchanged at the end
It becomes part of the product
questions.explain: A catalyst is not used up and remains chemically unchanged after the reaction.

questions.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It increases the concentration of reactants
questions.explain: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

questions.q: The symbol ⇌ in an equation shows that the reaction is:
questions.explain: The ⇌ symbol indicates a reversible reaction.

questions.q: Which method could be used to measure the rate of a reaction that produces a gas?
options: Measuring the colour of the flask
Measuring the volume of gas collected over time
questions.explain: Collecting and measuring the volume of gas produced over time gives the rate.

questions.q: If the concentration of a reactant is increased in a system at equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts to:
questions.explain: Adding more reactant shifts the equilibrium towards the products to oppose the change.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.
